correctness.rationale: At every finite state of the printed DAE the algebraic equation is e(t)(p x(t)-c)=m>0. From e(0)>0 it follows p x(0)-c>0; continuity of finite x and e and nonzero product prevent either factor crossing zero. Therefore throughout any finite continuous classical solution x(t)>c/p and e(t)>0. If it reached x=c/p, the exact algebraic equation would give 0=m, contradiction; the conclusion is independent of the delay dynamics. With source p=2500,c=.02,m=604.33, independently reduced exact rationals give c/p=1/125000, required effort at x=.2 =60433/49998 and at x=.8 =223/738; if caption initial triple is model order (x,y,e), the printed e=1.2 gives algebraic residuals -2177/500 and 897823/500 respectively. The primary published Figure 6 caption explicitly describes prey dying out from (.2,.5,1.2) and wildly fluctuating effort; those reported curves cannot be finite classical trajectories of this DAE if crossing the barrier or taking negative finite effort. An approximation may jump over the pole, and the initial-order interpretation is conditional; neither caveat alters the hard branch result.

value.rationale: A sharp viability restriction that invalidates a published model's claimed extinction simulation has scientific value: it distinguishes genuine biological extinction from numerical singularity crossing and exposes inconsistent initial data. The pole at c/p sets an explicit hard domain for admissible classical numerical integration and invalidates negative harvest effort from a positive branch; this is a substantive model-interpretation boundary rather than an arbitrary type/units check. No broad theory of DAE singularity is asserted.
